scenarios.expectedOutcome: An expired durable lease is reclaimed and the previous worker is fenced from acknowledging it.
Redelivery of the same indexing event is idempotent and does not repeat the completed projection side effect.
Expired work is reclaimable, poisoned work is quarantined, and causal descendants remain blocked until operator recovery.
Readiness fails while PostgreSQL is stopped and returns to UP after the service restarts.
Readiness reports raw object storage unavailable while MinIO is stopped and recovers after restart.
Readiness reports the extractor unavailable without treating the API process as live-dead, then recovers after restart.
An explicitly selected unavailable document-intelligence provider fails closed with a capability error.
Embedding writes with the wrong dimensions are rejected by both the lifecycle boundary and database invariant.
A stale embedding generation leaves normal selection and can enter a controlled rebuild lifecycle.
A graph revision that differs from the current corpus disables graph traversal and falls back to permitted channels.
Publication compensates or enters explicit recovery without emitting duplicate or premature durable events.
The core API remains live and ready when no MCP process is present because MCP is a consumer, not a runtime dependency.
The core API remains live and ready when the configured OpenTelemetry collector endpoint is unreachable.

limitations: Service restart probes exercise deterministic CI stop/start failures rather than long-duration network partitions or managed-service failover.
The post-side-effect crash case is scoped to the idempotent indexing consumer and does not claim exactly-once semantics for arbitrary external systems.
Provider unavailability is injected at the document-intelligence routing boundary.
The MCP scenario proves independence of the core API while MCP is absent; it does not emulate a connected MCP client losing its transport mid-request.
